feature: Data Model Enhancements for Multi-Provider Support
story: Define Core Provider and Model Types
story_description: As a developer, I need strongly-typed enums and structs representing AI providers, models, and tiers so that the codebase can safely route sessions to the correct CLI adapter and display accurate provider metadata in the UI.
task: Implement AIProvider, AIModel, ModelTier, and DirectorySource Types
task_description: Create the foundational Swift types (AIProvider enum, AIModel struct, ModelTier enum, DirectorySource enum) that represent provider metadata, model capabilities, and session initialization options. These types enable the harness to route sessions to the correct CLI adapter and display provider-specific branding.
atom_description: Add AIProvider enum (anthropic, openai, google, community), AIModel struct with full metadata (context window, costs, capabilities), ModelTier enum (flagship, balanced, fast), DirectorySource enum (browse, clone, create), and AIModelRegistry static lookup. Extend Session model with provider and modelId fields. Add database migration v7 for new columns.
problem_statement: The Session model currently lacks provider and model association fields needed for multi-CLI support. Without these, the harness cannot determine which CLI adapter to use, which model-specific CLI flags to pass, or which provider branding to display. This atom creates the type-safe foundation for the entire multi-engine architecture.

story_description: As a user, I want to clone a Git repository directly from the session creation flow so that I can start working on remote projects without leaving the app.
task_description: Add cloneRepository method to GitWorktreeManager that handles HTTPS and SSH URL cloning with progress reporting and error handling.
atom_description: Implement the core GitWorktreeManager.cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) method that spawns git clone as a child process, parses stderr for progress updates, handles authentication failures gracefully, and supports shallow cloning for faster setup.
problem_statement: Users currently can only browse existing local directories when creating sessions. There is no way to clone a remote Git repository directly from within the app, forcing users to switch to Terminal, clone manually, then return to Blaze to browse the cloned directory. This breaks workflow continuity and adds friction to the onboarding experience for new projects.
scope_in: Add cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) async method to GitWorktreeManager
Support HTTPS URLs in format https://github.com/owner/repo or https://github.com/owner/repo.git
Support SSH URLs in format git@github.com:owner/repo.git
Implement shallow clone option via --depth=1 flag for faster cloning of large repos
Parse git clone stderr output to extract progress phases: counting, compressing, receiving, resolving
Report progress percentage and phase via callback closure
Handle git clone exit codes and translate to typed GitError cases
Support cancellation via Task.checkCancellation() between progress updates
scope_out: Git LFS support - large file storage cloning deferred to future atom
Submodule handling - recursive submodule clone deferred to future atom
Custom authentication UI - rely on system git credential helpers and ssh-agent
Branch selection during clone - clone default branch only, branch switching is separate feature
Mirror or bare clone modes - not needed for user workflow
Clone to custom worktree - always clone to standard directory structure
assumptions: Git CLI is installed and available at /usr/bin/git or via PATH
System git credential helper is configured for HTTPS authentication
SSH agent is running and has appropriate keys loaded for SSH URLs
Destination parent directory exists and is writable
Network connectivity is available when clone is initiated
User has read access to the remote repository
constraints: Must use Process/NSTask to spawn git clone - cannot use libgit2 or other libraries
Progress parsing must handle both packed and unpacked progress output formats
Clone operation must be cancellable without leaving partial clone state
All git operations must run on background thread, not main thread
Memory usage must not grow unbounded during large clones
Timeout must be configurable with sensible default of 5 minutes
functional_requirements: FR1: cloneRepository shall accept a url parameter as String and validate it matches HTTPS or SSH URL patterns before proceeding
FR2: cloneRepository shall accept a destination parameter as String specifying the absolute path where the repository will be cloned
FR3: cloneRepository shall accept a shallow parameter as Bool defaulting to false that when true adds --depth=1 to the git clone command
FR4: cloneRepository shall accept a progress callback closure that receives CloneProgress struct updates during the clone operation
FR5: cloneRepository shall spawn git clone with --progress flag to ensure progress output is sent to stderr
FR6: cloneRepository shall parse stderr lines matching pattern 'Receiving objects: N%' and extract percentage as Int
FR7: cloneRepository shall parse stderr lines matching pattern 'Resolving deltas: N%' and extract percentage as Int
FR8: cloneRepository shall detect clone completion when git process exits with code 0 and .git directory exists at destination
FR9: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.invalidURL when url parameter does not match https:// or git@ patterns
FR10: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.authenticationFailed when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'Authentication failed'
FR11: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.repositoryNotFound when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'not found'
FR12: cloneRepository shall throw GitError.networkError when git exits with code 128 and stderr contains 'Could not resolve host'
FR13: cloneRepository shall clean up partial clone directory on failure before throwing error
FR14: cloneRepository shall respect Task cancellation and terminate git process when cancelled
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Clone operation must not block main thread - all Process spawning and I/O must be on background queue
NFR2: Progress callbacks must be delivered on MainActor for safe UI updates
NFR3: Memory usage during clone must remain constant regardless of repository size - stream stderr line by line
NFR4: Clone of 100MB repository over 100Mbps connection should complete within 30 seconds
NFR5: Error messages must be user-friendly and not expose raw git stderr when possible
implementation_steps: Step 1: Define CloneProgress struct with phase enum (counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done), percent Int, and message String
Step 2: Define ClonePhase enum with cases counting, compressing, receiving, resolving, done
Step 3: Add GitError cases: invalidURL(String), authenticationFailed(String), repositoryNotFound(String), networkError(String), cloneFailed(Int, String), cloneCancelled
Step 4: Create private helper parseCloneProgress(_ line: String) -> CloneProgress? that uses regex to extract phase and percentage from git stderr lines
Step 5: Create private helper validateCloneURL(_ url: String) throws that validates URL matches https:// or git@ patterns
Step 6: Add cloneRepository(url:destination:shallow:progress:) async throws -> String method signature to GitWorktreeManager
Step 7: In cloneRepository, first call validateCloneURL to check URL format
Step 8: Build git command arguments array: clone, --progress, optionally --depth=1, url, destination
Step 9: Create Process instance with executableURL pointing to git binary
Step 10: Configure Process with arguments array and empty environment to inherit system environment
Step 11: Create Pipe for stderr and assign to Process.standardError
Step 12: Create Task to read stderr pipe data in chunks and split into lines
Step 13: For each stderr line, call parseCloneProgress and if non-nil, dispatch progress callback on MainActor
Step 14: Check Task.isCancelled periodically and if true, call Process.terminate() and throw GitError.cloneCancelled
Step 15: Call Process.run() and Process.waitUntilExit() wrapped in withCheckedThrowingContinuation
Step 16: After process exits, check terminationStatus - if non-zero, parse stderr to determine specific error type and throw appropriate GitError
Step 17: If terminationStatus is 0, verify .git directory exists at destination, return destination path
Step 18: Add cleanup logic in catch block to remove partial clone directory via FileManager.default.removeItem

edge_cases: Empty URL string passed - throw GitError.invalidURL with message 'URL cannot be empty'
URL with trailing whitespace - trim whitespace before validation
URL with embedded spaces - throw GitError.invalidURL with message 'URL cannot contain spaces'
Destination directory already exists and is non-empty - git will fail, translate to GitError.cloneFailed with clear message
Destination directory already exists and is empty - git clone should succeed
Destination parent directory does not exist - throw GitError.cloneFailed before spawning git
Destination path is not absolute - throw GitError.cloneFailed with message 'Destination must be absolute path'
Repository requires authentication but credentials not available - throw GitError.authenticationFailed
Repository URL valid but repository deleted or private - throw GitError.repositoryNotFound
Network disconnected mid-clone - throw GitError.networkError after timeout
Clone cancelled while receiving objects - terminate git process, clean up partial directory
Very large repository (multiple GB) - shallow clone recommended, progress updates keep UI responsive
Repository with non-ASCII characters in name - URL encode properly
SSH URL with non-standard port - parse git@host:port:path format correctly
HTTPS URL with username embedded - support https://user@github.com/repo format
Git binary not found at expected path - throw GitError.cloneFailed with message 'Git not installed'
failure_modes: FM1: Git process spawn fails - FileManager cannot execute git binary. Handle by checking git exists before spawn, throw descriptive error.
FM2: Network timeout during clone - git hangs waiting for data. Handle by implementing 5-minute timeout that terminates process and cleans up.
FM3: Disk full during clone - git fails mid-write. Handle by catching clone failure, cleaning up partial directory, throwing GitError.cloneFailed with disk space hint.
FM4: Permission denied on destination - cannot create directory or files. Handle by pre-checking write permission before clone, throwing early with clear message.
FM5: SSH key passphrase required - blocking stdin prompt. Handle by setting GIT_SSH_COMMAND to use batch mode, detect passphrase errors in stderr.
FM6: Progress parsing fails - unexpected stderr format. Handle by continuing clone operation, deliver indeterminate progress updates.
FM7: Process terminated by system - SIGKILL or memory pressure. Handle by detecting non-zero exit without our cancellation flag, throw GitError.cloneFailed.
rollback_plan: To rollback this change: 1) Revert changes to GitWorktreeManager.swift and GitError.swift. 2) Remove any new test files. 3) Run swift build to verify compilation. 4) No data migration needed as this is additive functionality with no persistence changes.

story: Directory Source Selection for Session Creation
story_description: Users need to specify a working directory when creating a new session. The directory can come from three sources: browsing an existing local folder, cloning a remote Git repository, or creating a new empty project folder. This story enables all three workflows with a unified segmented picker UI.
task_description: Create the DirectorySourcePicker segmented control and its three conditional child views (BrowseDirectoryView, CloneRepositoryView, CreateProjectView) that allow users to specify the working directory for a new session.
atom: Directory Source Segmented Picker and Conditional Views
atom_description: Implement a segmented control with Browse, Clone, and Create segments. Each segment displays a distinct view: Browse shows a path display with NSOpenPanel trigger, Clone shows repository URL and destination inputs with progress indicator, Create shows project name input with parent folder selection and git init toggle. State persists across segment switches.
problem_statement: The current New Session modal only supports browsing for an existing directory. Users who want to clone a repository or create a new project folder must do so outside the app, then browse to that location. This friction discourages starting new projects directly from Blaze and creates extra steps in the workflow.
scope_in: Implement DirectorySourcePicker as a SwiftUI Picker with segmented style containing three cases: browse, clone, create
Implement BrowseDirectoryView with path display TextField (read-only) and Browse button that opens NSOpenPanel for directory selection
Implement CloneRepositoryView with TextField for repository URL, TextField for destination folder path, Toggle for shallow clone option, and ProgressView that appears during clone operations
Implement CreateProjectView with TextField for project name, read-only path display showing computed full path, Change button to select parent folder via NSOpenPanel, and Toggle for git init option
Define DirectorySource enum with associated values: browse(URL), clone(repositoryURL: String, destination: URL, shallow: Bool), create(name: String, parent: URL, initGit: Bool)
Preserve user input state when switching between segments so no data is lost
Validate Clone URL format using regex pattern for common Git URL formats (https, ssh, git protocol)
Show inline validation indicator (checkmark or X icon) next to Clone URL field based on format validity
scope_out: Template selection dropdown for Create mode (future enhancement)
Organization or team directory presets (future enhancement)
Actual git clone execution (handled by separate atom)
Actual directory creation execution (handled by separate atom)

problem_statement: The current NewSessionModal only supports browsing to an existing directory. Users cannot clone a remote repository or create a new project from scratch. Additionally, the modal has no way to select a provider (Claude, Gemini, Codex) or model before creating a session - it defaults to Claude. This atom integrates directory source types, provider selection, and model selection into a unified creation wizard.

atom_description: Implement the core routing logic in EngineManager that takes a Session and returns the appropriate EngineAdapter based on session.engineType, ensuring adapters are lazily registered and available before use.
problem_statement: EngineManager currently has a dictionary of adapters keyed by EngineType, but there is no method to get an adapter for a given Session. The orchestrator and UI need a single entry point that accepts a Session and returns the properly configured adapter for that session's provider.

story_description: As a user, I want to select from available CLI providers when creating a new session, with visual feedback when a CLI is not installed, so that I can quickly understand which providers are available and get guidance on installing missing ones.
task_description: Implement pre-flight validation that checks whether the selected provider CLI binary is installed and accessible on the system PATH before allowing session creation, with clear error states and installation guidance.
atom_description: Create CLIAvailabilityChecker service that detects installed CLIs via which/where commands, caches availability state, and integrates with NewSessionModal to disable unavailable providers and show install prompts.
problem_statement: Users may attempt to create a session with a provider whose CLI is not installed on their system. Without pre-validation, the app would fail at session spawn time with a confusing Process.run error. This atom implements proactive CLI detection to show availability status upfront, disable unavailable providers, and provide a clear path to installation.

problem_statement: Users must manually select their preferred provider every time they open the New Session modal. This creates friction for users who consistently use the same provider. story_description: As a developer, I need the core onboarding infrastructure (state machine, navigation, persistence) so that subsequent onboarding screens can be built on a solid foundation with consistent navigation and state management.
task_description: Create the OnboardingViewModel with step-based state machine, navigation logic, and AppStorage persistence for tracking onboarding completion and user selections.
atom_description: Implement OnboardingStep enum defining all wizard steps, OnboardingViewModel @Observable class with step navigation, validation, and persistence, and OnboardingRootView container with step-based content switching.
problem_statement: The application needs a structured onboarding flow to guide first-time users through CLI detection, profile setup, and plugin/skill selection. Without core infrastructure, each screen would need to manage its own navigation and persistence, leading to inconsistent behavior and duplicated code.
scope_in: OnboardingStep enum with all seven wizard steps (welcome, userProfile, cliDetection, skillsRecommendations, pluginsRecommendations, agentsRecommendations, completion)
OnboardingViewModel @Observable class with currentStep state and navigation methods
Step validation logic via canProceedFromCurrentStep() method
Forward navigation via goToNextStep() with validation gate
Backward navigation via goToPreviousStep() without validation
Skip functionality via skipStep() for optional screens
Completion handler via completeOnboarding() that sets hasCompletedOnboarding flag
AppStorage persistence for hasCompletedOnboarding boolean flag
AppStorage persistence for userName and userEmail strings
AppStorage persistence for installedCLIs, selectedSkills, selectedPlugins, selectedAgents as JSON-encoded strings
OnboardingRootView container that switches content based on currentStep
OnboardingNavigationBar component with Back, Skip, and Next buttons
Progress indicator showing current step position (e.g., step 3 of 7)
scope_out: Individual screen implementations (WelcomeOnboardingView, UserProfileOnboardingView, etc.) - handled by O002-O007
CLI detection logic and process spawning - handled by O004-CLIDETECT
Plugin/skill/agent recommendation algorithms - handled by O005-O007
Network calls to fetch remote catalogs - handled by O005-O007
Theme customization for onboarding screens - uses existing theme system
Localization of onboarding strings - deferred to L10N epic
assumptions: SwiftUI @Observable macro is available (macOS 14+)
AppStorage can persist Set types when JSON-encoded
The app launches to onboarding if hasCompletedOnboarding is false
Existing BlazeApp entry point can conditionally show OnboardingRootView vs main ContentView
constraints: Must use @Observable pattern consistent with existing codebase (SessionStore, EngineManager)
Must not block main thread during persistence operations
Navigation must be keyboard-accessible (Tab navigation, Enter to proceed)
State changes must be immediate with no perceptible lag
OnboardingStep raw values must be stable integers for persistence compatibility
functional_requirements: OnboardingStep enum defines exactly seven steps in fixed order: welcome(0), userProfile(1), cliDetection(2), skillsRecommendations(3), pluginsRecommendations(4), agentsRecommendations(5), completion(6)
OnboardingViewModel.currentStep initializes to .welcome on fresh install
OnboardingViewModel.goToNextStep() advances currentStep by 1 if canProceedFromCurrentStep() returns true
OnboardingViewModel.goToNextStep() does nothing if canProceedFromCurrentStep() returns false
OnboardingViewModel.goToPreviousStep() decrements currentStep by 1, minimum bound at .welcome
OnboardingViewModel.skipStep() advances to next step without validation (for optional screens)
OnboardingViewModel.canProceedFromCurrentStep() returns true for .welcome step (no requirements)
OnboardingViewModel.canProceedFromCurrentStep() returns true for .userProfile step if userName is non-empty OR if user explicitly chose to skip
OnboardingViewModel.canProceedFromCurrentStep() returns true for .cliDetection step if at least one CLI is detected/installed
OnboardingViewModel.completeOnboarding() sets hasCompletedOnboarding to true and persists all selections
OnboardingRootView renders the appropriate screen view based on currentStep value
OnboardingNavigationBar shows Back button when currentStep is not .welcome
OnboardingNavigationBar shows Skip button for steps marked as skippable (.userProfile, .skillsRecommendations, .pluginsRecommendations, .agentsRecommendations)
OnboardingNavigationBar shows Next button with enabled/disabled state based on canProceedFromCurrentStep()
Progress indicator displays current step number and total steps count
nonfunctional_requirements: State transitions complete in under 16ms to maintain 60fps UI
AppStorage writes complete in under 50ms
Memory footprint of OnboardingViewModel under 1KB
No retain cycles in @Observable bindings
Accessibility: VoiceOver announces step changes and button states

User clicks Back button: triggers goToPreviousStep(), returns to previous step
User clicks Skip button: triggers skipStep(), advances without validation

User presses Escape key: triggers Back button action (keyboard shortcut)

edge_cases: User force-quits during onboarding: AppStorage persists currentStep, resumes on relaunch

User at .completion clicks Next: completeOnboarding() is idempotent, safe to call multiple times

VoiceOver user navigates: all buttons have accessibility labels, step changes announced
failure_modes: AppStorage write fails (disk full): Log error, continue in-memory, retry on next interaction

OnboardingStep rawValue out of bounds: Default to .welcome, log unexpected state
Memory pressure during onboarding: No large allocations, graceful under low memory
SwiftUI view crash: Wrap in error boundary (if available), show fallback UI

story_description: As a new user launching Blaze for the first time, I want to see a welcoming screen that introduces the app and guides me to get started, so I feel confident and oriented.
task_description: Build the WelcomeOnboardingView SwiftUI screen with animated logo, headline, value proposition bullets, and Get Started CTA button.
atom_description: Create the first onboarding screen featuring an animated Blaze logo with scale and fade effects, a welcome headline, three value proposition bullet points, and a Get Started button that advances the onboarding flow.
problem_statement: New users opening Blaze for the first time have no context about what the app does or how to begin. Without a welcome screen, users land directly into the main interface feeling disoriented, which increases abandonment and reduces engagement.
scope_in: WelcomeOnboardingView.swift SwiftUI view file
Animated Blaze logo with scale and fade animation lasting 1.2 seconds
Welcome to Blaze headline text with appropriate typography
Three value proposition bullet points explaining app benefits
Get Started primary button that advances to the next onboarding screen
Accessibility support for reduced motion preference
Integration with OnboardingCoordinator for navigation flow

Localization for non-English languages (future enhancement)

story_description: As a new user, I want to enter my name and optional email during onboarding so that the app can personalize my experience and greet me by name on subsequent launches.
task_description: Build the UserProfileOnboardingView SwiftUI screen with first name, last name, and optional email fields, including validation, persistence to AppStorage, and welcome back toast functionality.
atom_description: Create a complete SwiftUI view for collecting user profile information during onboarding, with real-time field validation, skip functionality, AppStorage persistence, and personalized welcome toast on subsequent launches.
problem_statement: New users have no way to personalize their Blaze experience. The app cannot greet users by name or remember their identity across sessions, resulting in a generic and impersonal experience that fails to build user engagement.

Next button that validates and persists profile data to AppStorage

Account creation or cloud sync of profile data
Social login integration (Apple ID, Google, etc.)

constraints: Must use AppStorage for persistence (not UserDefaults directly) for SwiftUI binding

story_description: Users launching Blaze for the first time need guided onboarding that detects installed AI CLIs, offers one-click installation for missing ones, and configures the environment automatically so they can start coding immediately.
task_description: Implement the CLI detection screen that scans the system for installed AI CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Aider, OpenCode, Amp), displays their status with version info, and provides one-click installation for missing CLIs via Homebrew, npm, or pip.
atom: CLI Detection Screen with Installation Flow
atom_description: A SwiftUI view that presents a list of supported AI CLIs with their installation status, version numbers when installed, recommended badges, and one-click install buttons that orchestrate dependency checking, package installation, PATH configuration, and verification.
problem_statement: Users may not have all AI CLIs installed when they first launch Blaze, and manually installing command-line tools requires terminal knowledge, dependency management, and PATH configuration. This creates friction in the onboarding experience and may prevent users from using all supported engines.
scope_in: Detect installed CLIs by executing 'which' and version commands for each supported CLI
Display CLI cards showing name, icon, installed/not-installed status, and version when available
Show 'Recommended' badges for Claude Code and Aider based on capabilities
Provide 'Install' button for each missing CLI that triggers installation flow
Implement 'Install All Missing' bulk action button
Check runtime dependencies (Node.js, Python, Rust) before CLI installation
Install missing dependencies via Homebrew automatically
Execute appropriate package manager command (npm, pip, brew) per CLI
Update PATH in shell config file (.zshrc) after installation
Verify installation succeeded by re-running detection
Handle skip action to proceed without installing missing CLIs
scope_out: Authentication or login flows for any CLI - deferred to later screens
CLI configuration beyond PATH setup - handled in subsequent onboarding steps
Updating already-installed CLIs to newer versions - deferred to settings
Custom CLI path configuration - advanced users can configure manually
Windows or Linux support - macOS only for MVP
assumptions: Homebrew is installed or user will install it when prompted
Users have internet connectivity for package downloads
Shell is zsh with config in ~/.zshrc (macOS default since Catalina)
Supported CLIs publish version flags that return clean version strings
npm, pip, and brew commands are available after dependency installation
constraints: Must not require sudo password for standard installations
Must timeout detection commands within 5 seconds to avoid UI freezing
Must not modify PATH if CLI is already accessible
Must show progress feedback during installation (not just spinner)
Must support cancellation of in-progress installations
Installation must be atomic - partial installs should be cleaned up on failure
functional_requirements: FR1: On view appear, execute parallel detection for all six supported CLIs using Process spawn with 5-second timeout
FR2: Display each CLI as a card with icon, name, status badge (Installed/Not Installed), version string when installed, and Recommended badge where applicable
FR3: Show Install button for each not-installed CLI that transitions to installing state with progress indicator
FR4: Install button tap triggers dependency check, then runs appropriate install command, then verifies installation
FR5: Provide Install All Missing button that queues all missing CLI installations in sequence with aggregate progress
FR6: Skip button navigates to next onboarding screen without blocking on missing CLIs
FR7: Next button navigates forward and is enabled only when at least one CLI is installed
FR8: Re-detect CLI status after each successful installation and update UI accordingly
FR9: Display error state with retry option if installation fails, including error message from stderr
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Detection phase completes within 3 seconds for all CLIs running in parallel
NFR2: UI remains responsive during detection and installation with no main thread blocking
NFR3: Installation progress updates at least every 500ms for user feedback
NFR4: Memory footprint for Process spawns stays under 50MB
NFR5: Support VoiceOver accessibility with proper labels for all interactive elements

Step 2: Define SupportedCLI enum with cases for claudeCode, geminiCLI, codexCLI, aider, openCode, amp including detection commands and install commands
Step 3: Create CLIDetectionResult model with properties: cli enum, isInstalled bool, version optional string, error optional string
Step 4: Implement CLIDetectionViewModel with Published array of detection results and detection/installation methods
Step 5: Create detectCLI async method that spawns Process with which command followed by version command, with 5-second timeout
Step 6: Implement detectAllCLIs using TaskGroup for parallel detection of all supported CLIs
Step 7: Create installCLI async method that checks dependencies, installs if missing, then installs target CLI
Step 8: Implement checkDependencies method that verifies node/python/rust based on CLI requirements
Step 9: Create installDependency method using brew install with progress parsing from stdout
Step 10: Implement runInstallCommand for each CLI type (npm install -g, pip install, brew install)

Step 12: Implement verifyInstallation by re-running detection and comparing results

Step 14: Create InstallProgressView showing current step, progress bar, and cancel button

atom: Skills Recommendations Screen with Remote Registry Integration
atom_description: A SwiftUI view presenting a searchable, filterable grid of skill cards populated from a remote JSON registry, dynamically filtered to show only skills compatible with the user's detected CLIs, supporting multi-select checkbox behavior, category filtering, popularity sorting, and navigation via Skip and Next buttons.
problem_statement: Users new to AI CLI tools may not know which skills (pre-built prompts, workflows, and configurations) are available or would benefit their workflow. Without curated recommendations filtered to their installed CLIs, users must manually discover and configure skills, reducing time-to-value and increasing onboarding friction.
scope_in: Fetch skill metadata from remote registry endpoint (JSON over HTTPS)
Parse skill registry response into local SkillCard models with id, name, description, category, for_cli array, stars count, downloads count, and recommended flag
Display skills in a responsive grid layout with 2-3 columns based on window width
Filter displayed skills to only those matching at least one installed CLI from previous detection screen
Implement text search filtering across skill name and description fields
Implement category filter dropdown with All plus unique categories from registry
Sort skills by popularity using weighted score of stars and downloads
Display Recommended badge on skills flagged as recommended in registry
Implement checkbox selection state for each skill card with visual feedback
Track selected skills in view model for later installation
Provide Skip button that navigates forward without selecting any skills
Provide Next button that navigates forward and queues selected skills for installation
Show loading state while fetching registry data
Show error state with retry option if registry fetch fails
Cache registry response locally to avoid refetch on back navigation

Skill preview or detailed view modal - users see name, description, and badges only

Skill dependency resolution - skills are independent units

Must complete registry fetch and initial render within 5 seconds on typical network
Must handle registry unavailability gracefully with informative error state
Must preserve selection state if user navigates back and forward

story_description: Users launching Blaze for the first time need guided onboarding that detects installed AI CLIs, offers one-click installation for missing ones, and configures the environment automatically so they can start coding immediately.
task_description: Implement the Plugins Recommendations Screen that displays plugin recommendations grouped by CLI, dynamically filtering to only show sections for installed CLIs, with plugin cards containing install buttons for each recommended extension.
atom: Plugins Recommendations Screen with Dynamic CLI-Based Filtering
atom_description: A SwiftUI view that presents plugin recommendations organized by CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Aider), dynamically showing only sections for CLIs the user has installed. Each plugin is displayed as a card with name, description, install button, and status indicator. Installation triggers the appropriate package manager or opens external links for manual setup.
problem_statement: Users who have just installed AI CLIs may not know about useful plugins and extensions that enhance their workflow. Without guidance, they miss productivity improvements from tools like Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust for Claude Code, or official extension catalogs for Gemini CLI. The onboarding flow should surface these recommendations contextually based on which CLIs the user has installed.
scope_in: Display plugin recommendations grouped by installed CLI only
Show Claude Code plugins section when Claude Code is installed: Gastown, Continuous-Claude-v2, Braintrust
Show Gemini CLI section when Gemini CLI is installed: link to official extensions catalog
Show Codex CLI section when Codex CLI is installed: MCP servers info, AGENTS.md guide link
Show Aider section when Aider is installed: Git integration tips card
Render each plugin as a card with icon, name, description, and install/view action button
Track installation status per plugin (not installed, installing, installed)
Handle plugin installation via npm, pip, brew, or external URL opening
Persist plugin installation choices for session continuity
Provide Skip button to bypass plugin installation entirely
Provide Next button to proceed after reviewing recommendations
scope_out: Plugin configuration or settings after installation - deferred to CLI-specific settings
Auto-updating plugins to newer versions - manual process
Custom plugin discovery from registries - only curated recommendations shown
Plugin uninstallation from this screen - handled elsewhere if needed
Plugin compatibility validation - assume latest versions work
Cross-CLI plugin sharing or dependencies - each CLI section is independent
assumptions: User has completed CLI detection screen and OnboardingState contains installed CLI list
Plugin installation commands are stable and documented by plugin maintainers
External URLs for catalogs and guides are accessible and maintained
npm and pip are available in PATH after dependency installation in CLI detection screen
User has internet connectivity for plugin downloads and external links

Must not block UI during plugin installation - use async with progress feedback
Must handle offline gracefully - show plugins but disable install buttons with offline message
Plugin cards must be accessible with VoiceOver including install button state
Must complete render within 500ms regardless of number of plugins shown
External link opening must use NSWorkspace.shared.open for security

problem_statement: Users need to discover and select from available agent configurations during onboarding. ui_states: Inactive: Tutorial overlay not visible, TutorialViewModel.isActive is false
Active Step N: Overlay visible with spotlight on target N, callout showing step N content

Tap Previous button: Returns to previous tutorial step, disabled on first step

story_description: As a developer, I need onboarding and tutorial flows wired into the main app lifecycle so that first-time users see onboarding on launch, returning users see a welcome-back message, and users can access the tutorial overlay from anywhere in the app.
task: Wire Onboarding and Tutorial into BlazeApp Entry Point
task_description: Modify BlazeApp.swift and ContentView.swift to conditionally present OnboardingRootView as a fullScreenCover for first-time users, show TutorialOverlayView as an overlay when triggered, and display welcome-back toast for returning users with stored userName.
atom_description: Add @AppStorage bindings for hasCompletedOnboarding and userName, @State properties for showOnboarding, showTutorial, and showWelcomeBack, fullScreenCover modifier for OnboardingRootView, overlay modifier for TutorialOverlayView, onAppear logic to determine which flow to trigger, and environment object injection for OnboardingViewModel and TutorialViewModel.
problem_statement: The onboarding infrastructure (OnboardingRootView, OnboardingViewModel) and tutorial system (TutorialOverlayView, TutorialViewModel) exist as isolated modules. They must be wired into the main app entry point (BlazeApp.swift) to trigger automatically on first launch, resume if interrupted, show tutorial on demand, and welcome returning users by name. Without this integration, users would see the main app immediately without setup guidance.

feature: E005-F004: HookProvider Enum and Provider Abstraction
story: E005-F004-S001: Implement HookProvider enum for multi-CLI hook support
story_description: As a developer integrating multiple CLI tools, I need a unified HookProvider enum that encapsulates provider-specific configuration paths, event definitions, and capability flags so that the hooks system can seamlessly support Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and future providers without scattered conditionals.
task: E005-F004-S001-T001: Create HookProvider enum with provider properties
task_description: Implement the HookProvider Swift enum with cases for claude, gemini, and codex. Include computed properties for supportsHooks, configDirectoryName, settingsFilename, and events array that returns provider-specific HookEventDefinition collections.
atom_description: Create the foundational HookProvider enum in Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookProvider.swift that defines provider cases and their associated configuration. This enum serves as the single source of truth for provider-specific hook capabilities and paths throughout the application.
problem_statement: The current hooks implementation is Claude-specific with hardcoded paths and event types. To support Gemini CLI and OpenAI Codex CLI, we need a provider abstraction that encapsulates: (1) whether the provider supports hooks at all, (2) the config directory name for that provider, (3) the settings filename convention, and (4) the available hook events for each provider. Without this abstraction, adding new providers would require scattered conditionals throughout the codebase.

Implement supportsHooks computed property returning Bool based on provider capability
Implement configDirectoryName computed property returning provider-specific directory string
Implement settingsFilename computed property returning settings.json constant
Implement events computed property returning array of HookEventDefinition for each provider
Add Codable conformance for serialization in settings
Add CaseIterable conformance for UI iteration
Add RawValue String conformance for display and logging

story_description: As a developer building hooks, I need per-provider event type definitions so that the hook system validates events correctly for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI, and I can write type-safe hook handlers that know which events and matchers are available for each provider.
task_description: Define HookProvider enum, HookEventType per-provider enums, HookMatcher patterns, and HookCapability structs in HookSchema.swift that encode the complete event vocabulary for each supported CLI provider including blocking capabilities and matcher patterns.
atom_description: Create comprehensive Swift type definitions in HookSchema.swift encoding all hook event types for Claude Code (12 events), Gemini CLI (11 events), and Codex CLI (2 notify events), including which events support blocking, which matchers are valid per event, and tool name mappings between providers.
problem_statement: The hook system currently has no type-safe representation of which hook events exist for each CLI provider. Without per-provider event definitions, the hook builder cannot validate event names, cannot filter matchers appropriately, cannot indicate which events support blocking responses, and cannot support cross-provider hook migration with correct event name mapping.
scope_in: HookProvider enum with cases claude, gemini, codex representing supported CLI providers

ClaudeHookEventType enum with 12 events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, Notification, PermissionRequest, ErrorOccurred, ContextCompacted

story: E005-F004-S001: Create actor service for cross-provider hook management
story_description: As a Blaze developer, I need an actor-based service that manages hook configurations across multiple agentic CLI providers (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) so that hooks can be loaded, saved, merged, and resolved correctly for each provider context.
task_description: Implement the four core methods of MultiProviderHooksService: resolveConfigPath for provider-specific paths, loadHooks for async configuration loading, saveHooks for persisting configurations, and getEffectiveHooks for resolving merged configurations.
atom_description: Create the MultiProviderHooksService actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/MultiProviderHooksService.swift with Swift actor isolation, implementing resolveConfigPath, loadHooks, saveHooks, and getEffectiveHooks methods that handle provider-specific hook configuration management with proper error handling and thread safety.
problem_statement: Blaze currently lacks a centralized service to manage hook configurations across multiple CLI providers. Each provider stores hooks in different paths and formats (Claude uses .claude/settings.json, Gemini uses .gemini/settings.json, Codex uses .codex/config.toml). Without a unified service, the UI cannot load, display, edit, or save hooks for different providers, and there is no way to merge project-level hooks with worktree-specific overrides.
scope_in: Swift actor definition with proper isolation semantics
resolveConfigPath method returning provider-specific config URL based on provider enum, scope enum, and optional worktree ID
loadHooks async throwing method that reads and parses provider-specific config files into unified HookConfiguration model
saveHooks async throwing method that writes HookConfiguration back to provider-specific format and path
getEffectiveHooks method that merges global, project, and worktree hooks in correct precedence order
Error enum for service-specific failures (fileNotFound, parseError, writeError, invalidProvider)
Integration with existing HookConfiguration and HookNode models from H001-MODELS
Support for all three providers: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Config file exists but is empty - return HookConfiguration with empty hooks dictionary
Edge case 2: Config file has valid JSON but wrong schema - throw parseError with descriptive message including expected vs actual structure
Edge case 3: Config file path has spaces or special characters - URL must handle encoding correctly
Edge case 4: Worktree ID provided but worktree directory no longer exists - throw fileNotFound with worktree context in error
Edge case 5: Concurrent loadHooks and saveHooks for same provider - actor isolation ensures serialization
Edge case 6: saveHooks called while another process holds file lock - retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times then throw writeError
Edge case 7: Config file is symlink - follow symlink and operate on target file
Edge case 8: Global scope path differs per OS (macOS vs future Linux) - use appropriate path resolution
Edge case 9: Codex TOML config has nested tables not supported by basic TOML parser - throw parseError with suggestion to simplify config
failure_modes: File system permission denied on read - throw HooksServiceError.fileNotFound with permission context in description
File system permission denied on write - throw HooksServiceError.writeError with permission context
JSON parse failure - throw HooksServiceError.parseError with line number if available from decoder
TOML parse failure - throw HooksServiceError.parseError with TOML-specific error message
Directory creation failure - throw HooksServiceError.writeError with parent directory path
Disk full during atomic write - throw HooksServiceError.writeError and ensure temp file is cleaned up
Task cancelled during async operation - throw CancellationError without leaving partial state
rollback_plan: If MultiProviderHooksService causes issues: 1) Revert the file addition, 2) Remove any references added to existing files, 3) The hooks builder can fall back to direct file operations as before. No persistent state changes are made by this service that would require data migration on rollback.

story_description: As a user managing hooks across multiple CLI tools, I need a provider selector UI in the Hooks Builder so that I can switch between Claude Code, Gemini, and Codex hook configurations and see which events are available for each provider.
task_description: Create ProviderSelectorView.swift with a segmented control allowing users to select the target CLI provider for hook configuration, showing available events per provider and disabling unsupported providers with explanatory tooltips.
atom_description: Implement a segmented picker control at the top of the Hooks Builder interface that allows switching between Claude Code (12 events), Gemini (11 events), and Codex (disabled with tooltip). The selector must update the hook canvas to show only events valid for the selected provider and persist the selection across sessions.
problem_statement: The Hooks Builder currently assumes Claude Code as the only target provider. With multi-CLI support, users need to select which provider they are configuring hooks for. Different providers support different hook events (Claude has 12, Gemini has 11, Codex has its own set). Without a provider selector, users cannot create provider-specific hook configurations or understand which events are available for their target CLI.

story_description: Enable users to create hooks once and migrate them between different agentic CLI providers (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) with automatic event and tool name translation
task_description: Implement the HookMigrator struct that translates hook definitions between providers by mapping event names, tool names, and configuration formats while preserving hook semantics
atom_description: Build the HookMigrator struct with three core methods: migrateHook() for full hook translation, mapEventName() for event lifecycle mapping between providers, and mapToolName() for provider-specific tool name resolution
problem_statement: Users who configure hooks for one agentic CLI (e.g., Claude Code) cannot reuse those configurations with other CLIs (e.g., Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) because each provider uses different event names, tool names, and configuration formats. This forces users to manually recreate their hook setups for each provider, leading to duplication, inconsistency, and wasted effort.

story_description: Users designing hooks in the Blaze Hooks Builder need to export their configurations to the correct provider-specific config paths so that the target CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex CLI) can load and execute the hooks during agentic sessions.
task_description: Implement the HooksInstallationService that exports hook configurations to the correct provider-specific paths: Claude to .claude/settings.json, Gemini to .gemini/settings.json, and Codex to .codex/config.toml (TOML format). Handle path resolution, format conversion, file merging with existing configs, and atomic write operations.
atom_description: A Swift actor service (HooksInstallationService) that takes a HookConfiguration from the Hooks Builder, determines the target provider, resolves the correct config directory path relative to the project root, converts the hook data to the provider's native format (JSON for Claude/Gemini, TOML for Codex), merges with any existing configuration without overwriting unrelated settings, writes atomically using temporary file plus rename, and reports success or failure with detailed error messages.
problem_statement: The Blaze Hooks Builder creates hook configurations in a normalized internal format, but each CLI vendor expects hooks in different locations and potentially different formats. Without provider-specific export logic, users would have to manually create config directories, convert formats, and merge hook entries by hand, defeating the purpose of the visual builder. Additionally, careless writes could overwrite existing user configurations or leave partial files on error.
scope_in: Determine target config directory based on HookProvider enum (claude -> .claude/, gemini -> .gemini/, codex -> .codex/)
Resolve config directory path relative to project root URL from SessionStore or user selection
Create config directory if it does not exist (mkdir -p equivalent)
Convert HookConfiguration to provider-native JSON structure for Claude Code settings.json
Convert HookConfiguration to provider-native JSON structure for Gemini CLI settings.json
Convert HookConfiguration to TOML format for Codex CLI config.toml
Load existing config file if present to preserve non-hook settings (permissions, model preferences, etc.)
Deep merge hook entries with existing hooks section, replacing entries with matching descriptions or event+matcher combos
Write to temporary file first, then atomic rename to final path for crash safety
Return ExportResult with success/failure, path written, and any warnings about merged entries
Emit telemetry events for export attempts, successes, and failures
Handle Codex special case where hooks are limited to notify events only
scope_out: Actually executing hooks - that is HookRunner's responsibility in separate atom
Validating hook command syntax or testing if commands exist on PATH
Managing hook lifecycle (enable/disable) - handled by MultiProviderHooksService
Worktree-specific overrides - separate atom H009-CONTEXT handles worktree scope
UI for export action - ProviderSelectorView and ExportButton are separate atoms
Hook migration between providers - H007-MIGRATE handles conversion logic

story_description: Users designing hooks in the Blaze Hooks Builder need to export their configurations to the correct provider-specific config paths so that the target CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex CLI) can load and execute the hooks during agentic sessions.
task_description: Implement session-aware hook context by passing the active session's provider to the HookRunner, enabling hooks to execute with knowledge of which CLI engine is currently active and allowing provider-specific hook behavior without requiring hooks to detect the engine themselves.
atom_description: A Swift implementation that connects SessionStore session lifecycle events to HookRunner provider context, creating a HookProvider from the session's engineType when a session starts and setting it as the active provider on the HookRunner instance, enabling all subsequent hook executions to access provider-specific context for conditional logic and provider-aware behaviors.
problem_statement: Hooks executing during agentic sessions have no way to know which CLI engine (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) is currently active. This forces hook authors to implement their own engine detection logic, leading to duplicated detection code across hooks, potential detection failures when CLI output formats change, and inability to leverage the session context that Blaze already maintains. Without session-aware hook context, hooks cannot implement provider-specific behaviors reliably.

story: E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI type definitions and installation infrastructure
story_description: As an onboarding user, I need the app to understand different agentic coding CLIs (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Aider, Cursor, Cody, OpenCode, Amp) with their executable paths, version flags, dependencies, and install commands so that automatic detection and installation can proceed without manual configuration.
task: E005-F005-S001-T001: Create CLITypes.swift with CLI type definitions
task_description: Implement the foundational CLIType enum and supporting types (DependencyType, InstallCommand) in CLITypes.swift. The CLIType enum must define all supported CLI tools with computed properties for displayName, executable, versionFlag, description, isRecommended, dependencies array, and installCommand. This provides the data model for the entire CLI detection and installation subsystem.
atom_description: Create CLITypes.swift containing the CLIType enum with eight cases (claude, codex, gemini, aider, cursor, cody, opencode, amp) and comprehensive computed properties for each. Also define DependencyType enum for runtime prerequisites and InstallCommand enum for installation method variants. This atom is the foundation of the CLI installation service - all detection, installation, and UI components depend on these type definitions.
problem_statement: The onboarding flow needs to detect which agentic coding CLIs are installed and offer to install missing ones. Currently there is no unified model for CLI tools - we need a type-safe enum that captures: (1) the executable name for shell detection, (2) version flag for checking installation, (3) human-readable display name and description, (4) whether the tool is recommended for new users, (5) runtime dependencies like Node.js or Python, and (6) the appropriate install command (npm, pip, brew, etc.). Without this model, detection and installation logic would be scattered and inconsistent across the codebase.

story: E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI detection and installation infrastructure
story_description: As a first-time Blaze user, I need the app to automatically detect which agentic coding CLIs are already installed and offer to install missing ones during onboarding so that I can start using the app without manual CLI setup.
task_description: Implement the CLIInstallationService Swift actor that provides async methods for detecting installed CLIs, checking dependencies, and executing installation commands. The service must be thread-safe, cancellable, and emit progress events.
atom_description: Create the CLIInstallationService actor in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Services/CLIInstallationService.swift that orchestrates CLI detection and installation. This actor is the core business logic layer for the CLI setup feature, coordinating between CLIType definitions, shell command execution, and progress reporting.
problem_statement: Blaze needs to detect and install multiple agentic coding CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, etc.) during onboarding. Each CLI has different detection methods (checking PATH, version commands), dependencies (Node.js, Python, Rust), and installation mechanisms (npm, pip, brew, shell scripts). Without a centralized service actor, this logic would be scattered across view models and views, making it untestable, non-thread-safe, and difficult to maintain. The service must handle concurrent detection of multiple CLIs, sequential installation with progress tracking, cancellation support, and graceful error recovery.

edge_cases: Edge case 1: CLI executable exists but version command fails - return isInstalled=true with version=nil
Edge case 2: CLI partially installed (executable exists but broken) - detect as installed, installation will overwrite
Edge case 3: Network timeout during npm/pip install - throw CLIInstallError.timeout with 5-minute threshold
Edge case 4: User cancels during download phase - check isCancelled flag and throw .cancelled
Edge case 5: Permission denied during global npm install - throw CLIInstallError.permissionDenied
Edge case 6: Homebrew not installed for brew formula - throw CLIInstallError.dependencyMissing(.homebrew)
Edge case 7: Multiple CLIs with shared dependency (Node.js) - check dependency once and cache result
Edge case 8: PATH does not include Homebrew paths - search common Homebrew locations directly
Edge case 9: Version string in unexpected format - capture raw string, do not parse
Edge case 10: Empty types array passed to installMultipleCLIs - return empty report immediately
failure_modes: FM-001: Process.run() throws if executable not found - Mitigation: Catch and convert to CLIInstallError.notFound
FM-002: Shell command hangs indefinitely - Mitigation: Use Task.sleep with timeout and terminate process
FM-003: Race condition on isCancelled flag - Mitigation: Actor isolation ensures serial access
FM-004: Memory leak from Process not terminated - Mitigation: Always call terminate() in defer block
FM-005: progressSubject subscriber not cleaned up - Mitigation: Use AnyPublisher wrapper, no strong refs
FM-006: CLIType.installCommand returns .shell with malicious script - Mitigation: Only execute known commands from CLIType enum

story_description: As a user installing CLIs during onboarding, I need a robust state machine that tracks scanning, detection, installation progress, completion, skip, and error states so that the UI can accurately reflect what is happening and recover gracefully from failures
task_description: Create CLISetupState enum with all installation states (scanning, detected, installing, complete, skipped, error) and InstallProgress struct for tracking individual CLI installation progress
atom: A001: CLISetupState Enum and InstallProgress Implementation
atom_description: Define CLISetupState enum with six cases (scanning, detected, installing, complete, skipped, error) each carrying appropriate associated values, plus InstallProgress struct with downloadProgress, verifyProgress, installProgress, and currentStep properties
problem_statement: The CLI installation flow requires a deterministic state machine to coordinate UI updates, prevent invalid transitions, enable pause/resume/cancel, and provide clear error recovery paths. Without explicit state modeling, the UI would need to infer state from multiple boolean flags leading to impossible state bugs.
scope_in: CLISetupState enum with six cases: scanning, detected, installing, complete, skipped, error
Associated values for detected (results array), installing (cli, progress, queue), complete (installed, failed), error (SetupError)
InstallProgress struct with downloadProgress (Double 0-1), verifyProgress (Double 0-1), installProgress (Double 0-1), currentStep (String)
Equatable and Hashable conformance for SwiftUI observation
State transition validation helpers (canTransitionTo, validNextStates)
Debug description for logging state transitions
scope_out: Actual installation logic (handled by CLIInstaller in separate atom)
Network requests (handled by InstallationNetworkService)
UI rendering of states (handled by CLISetupView)
Persistence of state (in-memory only, restart resets to scanning)
Retry logic orchestration (handled by CLISetupViewModel)

feature: E005-F005: CLI Detection and Installation Views
story: E005-F005-S001: Implement CLI setup views for onboarding flow
story_description: As a new user setting up Blaze, I need a clear CLI setup view that displays detection status for each supported CLI tool and provides one-click installation so that I can quickly configure my development environment without manual terminal commands.
task_description: Implement the OnboardingCLISetupView SwiftUI view that displays CLI detection results in a card-based layout, shows installation status badges, provides install buttons for missing CLIs, and integrates with CLISetupViewModel for state management and action dispatch.
atom_description: Create the OnboardingCLISetupView.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/Views/ that renders the CLI detection screen with status cards for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider, OpenCode, and Amp. The view displays version info for installed CLIs, install buttons for missing ones, and recommended badges for suggested tools.
problem_statement: Users need a visually clear, actionable interface to understand which CLI tools are installed on their system and to install missing ones. Without this view, users would need to manually check terminal installations and run package manager commands, creating friction in the onboarding experience. The view must handle multiple CLI states (installed with version, not installed, installing, failed) and provide consistent visual feedback.

edge_cases: Edge case 1: All six CLIs already installed - Hide Install All Missing button, enable Next immediately
Edge case 2: No CLIs installed - Show warning that at least one is required, disable Next until one installs
Edge case 3: Installation succeeds but version detection fails - Show Installed badge without version number
Edge case 4: Multiple CLIs installing simultaneously - Each card shows independent Installing state
Edge case 5: Network error during installation - Show Failed badge with offline-friendly error message
Edge case 6: User has non-standard CLI locations - Detection may miss installed CLIs, provide manual path entry option in future
Edge case 7: Window resized very narrow - Cards should stack vertically and remain usable at 600pt minimum width
Edge case 8: User rapidly taps Install on multiple CLIs - Queue installations, do not duplicate requests

FM-002: Infinite re-render loop from bad state binding - Mitigation: Use proper Equatable conformance on CLIItem, avoid view-side state mutations
FM-003: Main thread blocked by synchronous detection - Mitigation: ViewModel uses async/await, view only observes published properties
FM-004: Memory leak from strong reference cycle - Mitigation: ViewModel uses weak self in closures, view is struct value type
FM-005: Accessibility labels missing causes VoiceOver confusion - Mitigation: Add accessibilityLabel to all interactive elements in implementation checklist

story_description: As a user installing agentic coding CLIs, I need a clear visual progress view during installation so that I can monitor progress, understand what is happening, and cancel if needed.
task_description: Create InstallationProgressView SwiftUI component that displays step-by-step installation progress for CLI packages with cancel functionality, elapsed time, output log streaming, and error state handling.
atom_description: Implement a SwiftUI view that renders real-time CLI installation progress including: current step indicator with checkmarks for completed steps, animated progress bar for current operation, streaming terminal output preview, elapsed time counter, cancel button with confirmation, error state display with retry option, and success completion state with celebration animation.
problem_statement: During CLI installation which can take 30-120 seconds depending on network speed and package size, users need visual feedback to understand installation progress, see what step is currently executing, monitor for errors, and have the ability to cancel a stalled or unwanted installation. Without this view, users would see a blank or spinning state with no indication of progress or ability to intervene.

story_description: As a user setting up Blaze for the first time, I need an intelligent orchestrator that coordinates CLI detection, dependency checking, installation, and state management so that the onboarding flow is seamless and I can recover from errors gracefully.
task_description: Build the CLISetupViewModel ObservableObject that orchestrates the entire CLI detection and installation workflow, managing state transitions, coordinating with CLIInstallationService, and exposing reactive bindings to the SwiftUI views.
atom_description: Implement CLISetupViewModel as an ObservableObject that manages CLI setup state machine transitions, coordinates async detection and installation operations via CLIInstallationService, handles user actions like install/skip/retry, exposes Published properties for view binding, and ensures proper error recovery and cancellation support.
problem_statement: The CLI detection and installation flow requires complex state management across multiple async operations including scanning PATH for binaries, checking versions, installing dependencies, and installing CLIs. Without a dedicated ViewModel to orchestrate this flow, the view layer would contain business logic, state transitions would be error-prone, and testing would be difficult. Users need clear feedback during long-running operations and the ability to cancel or retry failed installations.
scope_in: Implement CLISetupViewModel as MainActor ObservableObject class
Expose Published properties for setupState, detectedCLIs, selectedCLIs, currentProgress, and errors
Implement startScan() method that triggers CLIInstallationService.detectAllCLIs()
Implement installSelected() method that queues and executes CLI installations
Implement installAll() method as convenience for installing all missing CLIs
Implement skip() method to bypass installation and proceed to next onboarding step
Implement cancel() method to abort in-progress installation operations
Implement retry() method to restart failed installations
Manage state machine transitions per CLISetupState enum
Handle dependency resolution before CLI installation
Expose computed properties for canProceed, isInstalling, hasErrors
Integrate with OnboardingStore for navigation state
Emit telemetry events for setup milestones and errors
Support cancellation via Swift Concurrency Task cancellation
scope_out: Actual CLI binary detection logic which lives in CLIInstallationService
UI rendering which lives in OnboardingCLISetupView and InstallationProgressView
Persistence of detected CLI state across app launches
CLI authentication or login flows
Custom CLI configuration or settings
Network layer implementation for downloading binaries
assumptions: CLIInstallationService actor is implemented and provides detectAllCLIs(), install(cli:), and checkDependencies(for:) methods
CLISetupState enum is defined with scanning, detected, installing, complete, skipped, and error cases
CLIDetectionResult struct contains cli type, installed status, version, and path
OnboardingStore exists and provides navigation methods like advanceToNextStep()
Swift Concurrency is available with MainActor for UI state management
The app targets macOS 14.0 or later supporting modern Swift concurrency
constraints: ViewModel must be MainActor to safely update Published properties from async contexts
State transitions must be atomic to prevent race conditions between user actions and async callbacks
Cancellation must properly clean up partial installations to leave system in consistent state
Memory management must avoid retain cycles between ViewModel and closures
Error messages must be user-friendly without exposing internal implementation details
Installation queue must process CLIs sequentially to avoid resource conflicts
functional_requirements: FR1: CLISetupViewModel conforms to ObservableObject protocol for SwiftUI binding
FR2: setupState Published property reflects current CLISetupState enum value
FR3: detectedCLIs Published array contains CLIDetectionResult for each supported CLI
FR4: selectedCLIs Published Set contains CLIType values user has selected for installation
FR5: currentProgress Published optional contains InstallProgress during active installation
FR6: errorMessage Published optional contains user-facing error description when in error state
FR7: startScan() transitions state to scanning then calls service and transitions to detected on completion
FR8: installSelected() validates selection non-empty then transitions to installing and processes queue
FR9: installAll() selects all missing CLIs and calls installSelected()
FR10: skip() transitions state to skipped and advances onboarding navigation
FR11: cancel() cancels active Task and transitions to detected state preserving partial results
FR12: retry() clears error state and re-attempts failed operation based on context
FR13: canProceed computed property returns true when at least one CLI is installed or user skipped
FR14: isInstalling computed property returns true when state is installing case
FR15: hasErrors computed property returns true when state is error case or failed array non-empty
FR16: toggleSelection(cli:) adds or removes CLI from selectedCLIs set
FR17: selectRecommended() populates selectedCLIs with CLIs where isRecommended is true
FR18: State transitions emit telemetry events via AnalyticsService
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: State transitions must complete within 16ms to maintain 60fps UI updates
NFR2: Scan operation must complete within 5 seconds for typical system with 8 CLI candidates
NFR3: Memory footprint must not exceed 10MB during installation queue processing
NFR4: Cancellation must respond within 100ms of user action
NFR5: ViewModel must be testable in isolation via dependency injection of services
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create CLISetupViewModel.swift file in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/ViewModels directory

Step 5: Add @Published var selectedCLIs: Set<CLIType> = [] property

Step 8: Add private let installationService: CLIInstallationService dependency
Step 9: Add private let onboardingStore: OnboardingStore dependency
Step 10: Add private let analytics: AnalyticsService dependency
Step 11: Add private var installTask: Task<Void, Never>? for cancellation support
Step 12: Implement init(installationService:onboardingStore:analytics:) with dependency injection
Step 13: Implement startScan() that sets state to scanning, awaits service.detectAllCLIs(), updates detectedCLIs, transitions to detected
Step 14: Add error handling in startScan() that transitions to error state with user-friendly message
Step 15: Implement installSelected() that validates selectedCLIs non-empty, creates installTask, processes queue sequentially
Step 16: In installSelected() loop, check for task cancellation between installations
Step 17: Update currentProgress during each installation step via service callbacks

Step 21: Implement cancel() that calls installTask?.cancel(), sets installTask to nil, transitions to detected state

edge_cases: EC1: User cancels scan before any results returned transitions to error state with Scan cancelled message
EC2: User cancels installation mid-queue preserves already-installed CLIs in detected results
EC3: All selected CLIs fail installation transitions to complete with empty installed and populated failed arrays
EC4: Network timeout during installation includes timeout details in failure reason
EC5: Disk full during installation captures specific error and suggests cleanup
EC6: User rapidly toggles selection during scan ignores toggles until scan completes
EC7: Service returns empty detection results shows No supported CLIs found message
EC8: Homebrew not installed prompts user to install Homebrew first
EC9: User lacks admin privileges for certain installs shows permission error with instructions
EC10: Background app refresh interrupts installation resumes on app foreground
failure_modes: FM1: CLIInstallationService throws during scan - catch error, transition to error state, log details, show user-friendly message
FM2: Individual CLI install fails but others succeed - continue queue processing, aggregate failures, show summary at end
FM3: Task cancelled during await - check Task.isCancelled after each await, clean up gracefully
FM4: Memory pressure during large installation queue - use autorelease pools, stream progress rather than buffer
FM5: Retain cycle from closure capturing self - use [weak self] in all async closures
FM6: Race condition between cancel and completion - use actor isolation to serialize state transitions
rollback_plan: If CLISetupViewModel causes issues, the OnboardingCLISetupView can fall back to directly calling CLIInstallationService methods synchronously with local state variables. The ViewModel is an organizational layer that can be bypassed without affecting core functionality. Remove ViewModel file and update view to use inline state management.

atom_description: Implement all registry data model types in Blaze/Sources/Registry/Models/RegistryModels.swift including RegistryResponse as the top-level container, SkillItem/PluginItem/AgentItem as Identifiable+Codable domain types, RegistryMetadata for author/license/repository info, RegistryPermissions for tool access requirements, and VersionConstraint for CLI version compatibility. Each type includes computed properties for validation and display formatting.
problem_statement: The Blaze app needs to consume a remote extension registry serving skills, plugins, and agents for multiple CLI tools. Without strongly-typed Swift models, JSON parsing would be ad-hoc and error-prone. The models must handle schema evolution, validate constraints, and provide a clean API for cache storage and UI rendering.

story_description: Implement the network layer responsible for fetching registry data from remote sources with proper error handling, signature verification, retry logic, and fallback URL support for reliability.
task_description: Create the network fetcher class that retrieves registry JSON from primary and fallback URLs, verifies Ed25519 signatures, handles network errors gracefully, and provides async/await API for downstream consumers.
atom_description: Implement RegistryFetcher as an actor in Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryFetcher.swift providing async methods to fetch registry data from Cogit0 API (primary) or GitHub Raw (fallback). Includes Ed25519 signature verification using CryptoKit, exponential backoff retry logic, request timeout handling, ETag-based conditional fetching for bandwidth efficiency, and structured error types for callers to handle gracefully.
problem_statement: The Blaze app needs to fetch extension registry data from remote servers securely. Without signature verification, a man-in-the-middle attack could inject malicious skills/plugins/agents. Without retry logic and fallback URLs, temporary network issues would prevent users from accessing the registry. The fetcher must balance security, reliability, and performance.

story_description: Implement a persistent SQLite cache layer for registry data that stores fetched skills, plugins, and agents locally with time-to-live expiration to reduce network requests, enable offline access, and provide fast startup times for the registry UI.
task_description: Create the SQLite-backed cache implementation with 24-hour TTL expiration, CRUD operations for registry items, cache invalidation logic, and migration support for schema evolution.
atom_description: Implement RegistryCache actor in Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryCache.swift providing SQLite-backed persistence for RegistryResponse data with 24-hour TTL expiration. The cache stores skills, plugins, and agents in normalized tables with foreign keys, supports atomic batch inserts, provides staleness checks via lastUpdated timestamps, implements cache invalidation on TTL expiry or manual refresh, and handles schema migrations for future changes. Uses SQLite.swift library for type-safe database operations.
problem_statement: The registry fetcher makes network requests to retrieve skills, plugins, and agents from remote sources. Without local caching, every app launch or UI refresh triggers network traffic, causes startup latency, and fails completely when offline. A SQLite cache with TTL expiration provides fast local reads, reduces API load, enables offline functionality, and maintains freshness through periodic re-validation.

story_description: Implement the file system operations layer that downloads, validates, and installs registry items (skills, plugins, agents) to their appropriate CLI-specific directories with atomic operations, rollback support, and progress reporting.
task_description: Create the RegistryInstaller actor that handles downloading registry items from URLs, verifying checksums, extracting archives, and installing files to CLI-specific directories with atomic move operations and rollback on failure.
atom_description: Implement RegistryInstaller actor in Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryInstaller.swift providing async install/uninstall operations for SkillItem, PluginItem, and AgentItem types. Includes download with progress reporting via AsyncStream, SHA256 checksum verification, ZIP archive extraction, atomic file operations using temporary staging directories, rollback on partial failure, and CLI-specific installation path resolution for claude-code (~/.claude/skills/), gemini-cli (~/.gemini/plugins/), and codex-cli (~/.codex/agents/). Exposes InstallationState enum for UI binding and emits telemetry events for installation analytics.
problem_statement: Users need to install skills, plugins, and agents from the remote registry to their local CLI configurations. Without a robust installer, downloads may be interrupted, files may be corrupted, or partial installations may leave the system in an inconsistent state. The installer must handle network failures, disk space issues, permission errors, and provide clear progress feedback to the UI.

rollback_plan: If installation fails after files are partially moved to target directory, the rollback method iterates through installedFiles array and removes each file. If rollback itself fails (permission denied, file locked), log error with file paths for manual cleanup. Temporary staging directory is always removed in defer block. UserDefaults manifest is only updated on successful completion so inconsistent state is impossible.
