story_description: Enable exporting hook configurations from the visual builder to various target formats, allowing users to share, backup, and deploy hooks across different CLI providers and plugin systems.
task_description: Create HookExportService actor that handles exporting hook configurations to multiple formats including Claude settings.json, Gemini settings.json, plugin hooks.json, and YAML frontmatter for agents/skills.
atom_description: Implement HookExportService actor with ExportFormat enum supporting claudeSettings, geminiSettings, pluginHooks, and frontmatter formats. Provides async export method with pre-export validation via HookValidator, format-specific exporters, and intelligent merging with existing settings files to preserve non-hook configuration.
problem_statement: Users who create hooks in the visual builder need to export them for actual use with CLI tools. Each CLI provider expects hooks in different formats: Claude uses .claude/settings.json with a hooks object, Gemini uses .gemini/settings.json with its own schema, plugins expect hooks.json with wrapper metadata, and agent/skill definitions use YAML frontmatter. Currently there is no unified export mechanism that validates configurations before export, handles format conversion correctly, and safely merges with existing settings files without clobbering non-hook configuration.

Safe file merging that reads existing file, updates only hooks section, preserves other keys
JSON output with prettyPrinted and sortedKeys options for human-readable output
Atomic file writes using write(to:) with atomic option to prevent partial writes

story_description: As a developer, I need a Swift adapter that communicates with the Codex app-server via bidirectional stdio JSON-RPC so that Blaze can send prompts and receive streaming responses without HTTP transport.
task: Build CodexStdioAdapter with Process pipe management
task_description: Create CodexStdioAdapter actor that spawns codex app-server process, writes JSON-RPC requests to stdin, reads JSON-RPC responses and notifications from stdout, correlates responses to pending requests via CheckedContinuation, and exposes an AsyncStream for notifications.
atom_description: Implement CodexStdioAdapter actor with: (1) spawn codex app-server with piped stdin/stdout/stderr, (2) atomic request ID counter, (3) pending request map keyed by ID with CheckedContinuation, (4) stdout reader task parsing newline-delimited JSON, (5) stdin writer for JSON-RPC requests, (6) AsyncStream of notifications for UI events, (7) graceful shutdown with SIGTERM then SIGKILL.
problem_statement: The current F008 architecture assumes HTTP transport for Codex communication, but CodexMonitor (the reference Tauri app) demonstrates that codex app-server uses stdio JSON-RPC. Without a proper stdio adapter, Blaze cannot integrate with Codex CLI. This atom creates the foundational bidirectional pipe communication layer that all higher-level Codex features will depend on.

Spawn codex app-server process with stdin/stdout/stderr pipes
Create AtomicInteger class for thread-safe request ID generation
Define pendingRequests dictionary mapping request ID to CheckedContinuation
Implement readLoop task that reads stdout line-by-line and parses JSON
Route JSON-RPC responses to matching pending continuation
Route JSON-RPC notifications to AsyncStream for subscribers
Implement sendRequest method that writes JSON-RPC to stdin and awaits response
Handle process termination and restart logic
Implement graceful shutdown with SIGTERM followed by SIGKILL timeout
scope_out: Codex protocol message types (defined in separate T002 atom)
High-level conversation API (deferred to S003)
Authentication and session management with Codex
Error recovery and automatic reconnection policies
Codex-specific tool call handling

codex app-server uses newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio
JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol with id field for request-response correlation
Notifications have null id field per JSON-RPC spec
Process can be terminated and restarted without state loss
constraints: Must use Swift concurrency (async/await) not completion handlers
Actor isolation required for thread-safe pending request map access

Must not block main thread during stdio operations

story_description: Parse and normalize the event stream from Codex app-server into NormalizedEvent types that the Blaze UI and hook system can consume, bridging the JSON-RPC protocol differences from the NDJSON format used by Claude Code.
task_description: Create CodexJSONRPCParser that reads raw JSON from app-server stdout and classifies each message as response, request, or notification based on JSON-RPC 2.0 field presence rules.
atom_description: Implement CodexJSONRPCParser struct that parses newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 messages, classifies them by type (response, request, notification), and routes them appropriately: responses to pending request handlers, requests to approval callback, and notifications to the event stream.
problem_statement: Codex app-server emits JSON-RPC 2.0 messages over stdio (newline-delimited JSON), not the NDJSON event stream format used by Claude Code. The JSON-RPC 2.0 spec defines three message types distinguished by field presence: responses have id + result or error, requests have id + method, and notifications have method but no id. Blaze needs a parser that correctly discriminates these message types and routes them to appropriate handlers. Malformed JSON must be handled gracefully without crashing.

JSONRPCMessage struct containing type, id, method, params, result, error fields
CodexJSONRPCParser struct with parse(line: String) method
Message classification logic based on field presence per JSON-RPC 2.0 spec
Extraction of Codex-specific method names (item/agentMessage/delta, turn/started, etc.)
Malformed JSON error handling with ParseError type

assumptions: App-server emits one JSON object per line (newline-delimited)
JSON-RPC 2.0 message format is stable across Codex versions
Field presence rules match JSON-RPC 2.0 spec exactly
Method names follow dot-notation hierarchy (turn/started, item/agentMessage/delta)
Result and error fields are mutually exclusive in responses
Params field is optional for both requests and notifications

Must handle partial or truncated JSON gracefully
Must not crash on unexpected field types or missing fields
Must preserve original JSON for logging and debugging
No third-party JSON parsing libraries; use Foundation JSONDecoder only
Must support all Codex method names discovered in CodexMonitor
functional_requirements: FR1: Parser shall accept a single line string and return a parsed JSONRPCMessage or ParseError
FR2: Parser shall classify message as response when id is present AND (result OR error is present)
FR3: Parser shall classify message as request when id is present AND method is present AND result/error are absent
FR4: Parser shall classify message as notification when method is present AND id is absent
FR5: Parser shall extract method name as String for requests and notifications
FR6: Parser shall extract id as either Int or String to match JSON-RPC 2.0 flexibility
FR7: Parser shall extract params as AnyCodable for downstream processing
FR8: Parser shall extract result as AnyCodable for response payloads
FR9: Parser shall extract error.code (Int), error.message (String), and error.data (AnyCodable?) for error responses
FR10: Parser shall return ParseError.invalidJSON when input is not valid JSON
FR11: Parser shall return ParseError.ambiguousMessage when classification rules are not met
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Parse latency shall be under 1ms for typical messages (under 10KB)
NFR2: Parser shall handle messages up to 1MB without memory issues
NFR3: Parser shall not allocate excessive memory for malformed input
NFR4: Parser must be thread-safe (stateless design)

Step 4: Define JSONRPCMessage struct with type (JSONRPCMessageType), id (JSONRPCId?), method (String?), params (AnyCodable?), result (AnyCodable?), error (JSONRPCError?) properties
Step 5: Define JSONRPCId enum with cases: int(Int), string(String) to handle both id types

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty string input - throws ParseError.invalidJSON
Edge case 2: Valid JSON but empty object {} - throws ParseError.ambiguousMessage
Edge case 3: Response with both result and error - classified as response, error takes precedence
Edge case 4: Message with id as Int (123) - extracted as JSONRPCId.int(123)
Edge case 5: Message with id as String (abc-123) - extracted as JSONRPCId.string(abc-123)
Edge case 6: Message with id as null - treated as no id (notification if method present)
Edge case 7: Notification with extra unknown fields - parsed successfully, extra fields ignored
Edge case 8: Method name with slashes (item/agentMessage/delta) - preserved exactly as string
Edge case 9: Very large params object (1MB JSON) - parsed if valid, may be slow
Edge case 10: Unicode in method name or string values - handled by JSONDecoder
Edge case 11: Trailing whitespace or newline - trimmed before parsing
Edge case 12: Multiple JSON objects on same line - only first is parsed
failure_modes: FM1: Invalid JSON syntax - returns ParseError.invalidJSON with decoder error message
FM2: Unexpected field types (id as array) - returns ParseError.ambiguousMessage
FM3: Memory exhaustion on huge input - limited by JSONDecoder, fails gracefully
FM4: Stack overflow on deeply nested JSON - limited by JSONDecoder recursion

story_description: Implement bidirectional JSON-RPC communication for Codex CLI tool approval requests. Unlike Claude Code which uses pre-approval via --allowedTools flags, Codex app-server sends runtime REQUESTS that require synchronous RESPONSES with matching IDs.
task: T004: CodexApprovalFlow - Tool Approval Request/Response Handling
task_description: Implement CodexApprovalFlow class that receives JSON-RPC tool approval requests from Codex app-server, maps them to ToolRiskLevel, integrates with ToolApprovalPipeline, and sends properly formatted JSON-RPC responses with matching request IDs.
atom_description: Build CodexApprovalFlow.swift handling codex/requestApproval/commandExecution and codex/requestApproval/fileChange JSON-RPC methods. Map commandExecution to high risk, fileChange to medium risk, others to low risk. Integrate with existing ToolApprovalPipeline for decision flow. Return JSON-RPC response with matching ID and decision accept/reject.
problem_statement: Codex app-server uses a fundamentally different approval model than Claude Code. Instead of pre-approving tools via CLI flags, Codex sends JSON-RPC REQUESTS at runtime asking for permission to execute commands or modify files. The client MUST respond with a JSON-RPC response containing the same request ID and a decision. Without this bidirectional protocol, Codex will hang waiting for responses. We need to: (1) parse incoming JSON-RPC requests, (2) map approval types to ToolRiskLevel for consistent UX, (3) integrate with ToolApprovalPipeline for user decisions, and (4) format and send JSON-RPC responses.

task_description: Implement the JSON-RPC initialization sequence required before any Codex operations can proceed
atom_description: Implement the mandatory app-server initialization handshake sequence: spawn process, send initialize request, await response, send initialized notification, await codex/connected notification
problem_statement: Codex CLI operates as a JSON-RPC server requiring a strict initialization handshake before accepting any operations. Without this handshake, the server ignores all requests. The sequence must be: (1) spawn process, (2) send initialize request with client info, (3) await initialize response within timeout, (4) send initialized notification, (5) await codex/connected notification. Failure at any step must abort with clear error.

Error handling for timeout, malformed response, or missing connected notification
scope_out: Actual operation execution (covered by separate atoms)
Session resume logic (separate handshake variant)
Authentication flow (handled before process spawn)
Process spawning mechanics (covered by ProcessRunner atom)

JSON-RPC messages are newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout
The initialize response contains server capabilities we can ignore for MVP
codex/connected notification arrives within reasonable time after initialized
constraints: Must follow JSON-RPC 2.0 specification for request/notification structure
Initialize request requires id field; initialized notification must not have id
Timeout must be configurable but default to 15 seconds
Must not send any operations until codex/connected received

task_description: Create CodexThreadManager class that wraps the four core thread JSON-RPC methods: thread/list to fetch all threads, thread/start to create new threads, thread/resume to restore existing threads, and thread/archive to archive threads. Filter threads client-side by workspace cwd. Store threadId in Session model.
atom_description: Implement CodexThreadManager actor with: (1) thread/list paginated fetching with cursor support, (2) client-side filtering by workspace.path matching thread.cwd, (3) thread/start with cwd and approvalPolicy params returning threadId, (4) thread/resume to restore thread with full turn history, (5) thread/archive to remove thread from active list, (6) threadId storage in Session model for continuity across app restarts.
problem_statement: Codex uses a workspace-to-thread hierarchy where each workspace can have multiple conversation threads. Threads are persisted server-side by Codex and must be fetched, filtered, and managed by the harness. Without CodexThreadManager, Blaze cannot list existing threads for a workspace, create new threads, resume previous conversations, or archive completed threads. This atom bridges the gap between Codex server-side thread storage and Blaze local session management.

atom: A001-CodexSandboxPolicyMapper Maps Blaze Security Modes to Codex Policies
atom_description: Implement CodexSandboxPolicyMapper struct with static methods to convert Blaze SecurityMode enum values to Codex-compatible sandboxPolicy and approvalPolicy JSON. Sandbox mode maps to readOnly type, Review mode maps to workspaceWrite type with writable project path and network access, Trusted mode maps to dangerFullAccess type. problem_statement: Blaze has a SecurityMode enum with three values (Review, Trusted, Sandbox) that govern file access and command approval. Codex uses different terminology with sandboxPolicy (readOnly, workspaceWrite, dangerFullAccess types) and approvalPolicy (on-request, never). Without a mapper, the CodexAdapter would need inline conversion logic that couples Blaze security concepts to Codex protocol details.

story_description: As a developer, I need a Swift adapter that communicates with the Codex app-server via bidirectional stdio JSON-RPC so that Blaze can send prompts and receive streaming responses without HTTP transport.
task_description: Extend NormalizedEvent enum with Codex-specific variants that map from Codex's unique streaming events (turn/plan/updated, account/rateLimits/updated, item/reasoning, item/commandExecution/outputDelta, item/fileChange/outputDelta) to enable full-fidelity rendering of Codex sessions.
atom_description: Add five new NormalizedEvent cases: TurnPlanUpdated (from turn/plan/updated with turnId, explanation, steps array), RateLimitsUpdated (from account/rateLimits/updated with primary/secondary RateLimit), ReasoningDelta (from item/reasoning/* with summaryDelta/contentDelta), ToolOutputDelta (from item/commandExecution/outputDelta), and FileDiffDelta (from item/fileChange/outputDelta). Each case includes associated data structs with proper Codable/Sendable conformance.
problem_statement: Codex CLI emits structured streaming events that have no equivalent in the current NormalizedEvent enum. Events like turn/plan/updated (showing multi-step execution plans), account/rateLimits/updated (quota tracking), item/reasoning/* (extended thinking), and incremental output deltas for commands and file changes cannot be represented with existing cases. Without these extensions, Blaze will either drop Codex-specific data or force it into ill-fitting generic containers, degrading the user experience.

story: Wire Codex Adapter to Session Orchestration
story_description: As a developer, I need the Codex adapter components wired into SessionOrchestrator and EngineManager so that Codex sessions use long-lived stdio processes instead of spawn-per-turn like Claude.
task_description: Modify SessionOrchestrator.executeTurn() to detect the session provider type and route Codex sessions to a shared long-lived CodexStdioAdapter instance per workspace, while Claude sessions continue using spawn-per-turn. Add codexThreadId and codexWorkspaceId fields to Session model. Update EngineManager to return appropriate adapter type based on provider.
atom_description: SessionOrchestrator.executeTurn() detects provider type from session. For Codex sessions, it uses a shared CodexStdioAdapter per workspace (long-lived process). For Claude sessions, it continues spawn-per-turn pattern. Session model gains codexThreadId and codexWorkspaceId optional fields. EngineRouter returns CodexStdioAdapter for .codex engine type. Includes process lifecycle management: start on first turn, reuse across turns, cleanup on session end.
problem_statement: Even with all Codex adapter components (CodexStdioAdapter, CodexEventMapper, CodexResponseParser) implemented, they are not wired into the Blaze session flow. SessionOrchestrator currently hardcodes Claude adapter usage. Codex CLI uses a fundamentally different interaction model: long-lived stdio process with JSON-RPC vs Claude spawn-per-turn with NDJSON. Without this wiring, Codex sessions cannot execute turns.

story_description: As a developer, I need stdio-based JSON-RPC communication with Codex CLI to stream assistant responses in real-time and accumulate incremental text deltas into complete messages.
task_description: Create a Swift Actor that accumulates item/agentMessage/delta events by itemId into complete text, emitting AssistantDelta events for UI streaming and AssistantComplete events when item/completed arrives.
atom: A001-CODEX-DELTA-ACCUMULATOR Actor for streaming text accumulation
atom_description: CodexDeltaAccumulator is a Sendable Swift Actor that maintains a dictionary mapping itemId (String) to accumulated text (String). On each item/agentMessage/delta event, it appends the delta text to the corresponding itemId entry and emits an AssistantDelta NormalizedEvent with the partial text. On item/completed event, it emits an AssistantComplete event with the full accumulated text, then removes the entry from the dictionary. Thread-safe by actor isolation, zero-copy where possible via String slicing.
problem_statement: Codex CLI streams text incrementally via item/agentMessage/delta JSON-RPC events, each containing a small text fragment for a specific itemId. The UI needs AssistantDelta events to render streaming text in real-time. When item/completed arrives, the full accumulated text must be emitted as AssistantComplete. Without an accumulator, the UI would either miss partial updates (batch mode) or lose track of which fragments belong to which message (no itemId correlation).

story_description: As a developer, I need the Codex adapter to communicate with the Codex CLI via stdio JSON-RPC so that long-lived sessions work correctly with streaming events and conversation resume.
task_description: On thread/resume, the Codex server returns stored items from the conversation history. Meanwhile, the local streaming buffer may have accumulated newer items during the resume request. CodexItemMerger deduplicates by itemId, keeping the richer version (more content) for each conflict. Handles the edge case where a streaming item arrives after resume completes.
atom: A001-CODEX-ITEM-MERGER Intelligent merge of resume vs streaming items
atom_description: CodexItemMerger provides merge(remote:local:) function that takes remote items from resume response and locally accumulated streaming items, returning a merged array with no duplicates. For each itemId present in both sets, the version with more content wins. Content richness is measured by: (1) presence of non-empty content field, (2) total byte length of serialized item, (3) presence of metadata fields. Handles race condition where streaming item arrives after resume response processing completes by exposing mergeIncremental(existing:newItem:) for single-item updates.
problem_statement: When resuming a Codex session, there is a race condition between the server response and local streaming. The resume RPC returns the canonical conversation history, but streaming events may have already accumulated locally (user sent a prompt, streaming started, then resume response arrives). Without intelligent merging, we either lose the streaming updates (if we replace with remote) or have duplicates (if we concatenate). This atom implements the merge algorithm that every-code uses: compare by itemId, keep the richer version.

story_description: As a developer, I need Blaze to communicate with Codex CLI via JSON-RPC over stdio so that all Codex protocol methods and events are supported.
task_description: Implement support for Codex review mode where the agent pauses for human review. Handle the review/start RPC method to initiate review, parse enteredReviewMode and exitedReviewMode events to track state, and integrate with turn lifecycle so review pauses the active turn until user approves or cancels.
atom_description: CodexStdioAdapter gains review mode support. The review/start JSON-RPC method initiates review pause. The enteredReviewMode event transitions session to review state with proposed changes. The exitedReviewMode event resumes normal execution. UI state tracks isInReviewMode to show review panel. Turn lifecycle is paused during review: no new events emitted until user action. User can approve (resume execution) or cancel (abort turn). ReviewModeState enum captures pending changes and context for UI display.
problem_statement: Codex CLI has a review mode feature where the agent pauses execution to allow human review of proposed changes before proceeding. Without handling this protocol, Blaze cannot support interactive approval workflows that are core to safe AI coding assistance. The review/start RPC initiates review, enteredReviewMode signals pause with pending changes, and exitedReviewMode signals resumption. These must integrate cleanly with existing turn lifecycle.

atom_description: Implement line-by-line diff algorithm that takes before (original) and after (modified) file content strings and produces FileDiff with hunks array compatible with DiffViewer and FilesSidebarView
problem_statement: Codex CLI item/fileChange events provide full before and after file content but Blaze FileDiffProduced events require unified diff format with hunks containing line additions, deletions, and context. Need an algorithm to compute the diff from raw content pairs without relying on external tools like git diff.
scope_in: Line-by-line diff computation from before/after string content
DiffHunk generation with oldStart/oldCount/newStart/newCount metadata
DiffLine generation with type (context/addition/deletion) and line numbers
Edge case handling for new files (empty before) and deleted files (empty after)
Async computation wrapper for large file performance
scope_out: Binary file diff support (text only for MVP)
Word-level or character-level diff highlighting
Git integration or external diff tool invocation
Diff patch application (handled by DiffService)
Syntax-aware diff merging
assumptions: Before/after content are UTF-8 encoded strings
Line endings are normalized (LF or CRLF handled consistently)
Files under 100KB do not require chunked processing
Context lines default to 3 lines above and below changes (standard unified diff)
constraints: Must produce DiffHunk format compatible with existing DiffViewer.swift
Algorithm must be pure Swift with no external dependencies
Computation must be async to avoid blocking main thread on large files
Output hunks must be contiguous (no overlapping line ranges)
functional_requirements: FR1: Accept before String, after String, and path String as input parameters
FR2: Split content into lines and compute longest common subsequence (LCS) or Myers diff
FR3: Generate DiffLine entries with correct type (context, addition, deletion) and line numbers
FR4: Group consecutive changes into DiffHunk objects with accurate oldStart/oldCount/newStart/newCount
FR5: Add configurable context lines (default 3) around each change group
FR6: Return FileDiff object with computed hunks and file path
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Diff computation for typical files (under 1000 lines) must complete in under 100ms
